claims.text: Pulse-controlled, block-copolymer-assisted dropwise synthesis will produce uniformly distributed ultrafine Pt nanoparticles on a high-entropy mixed-oxide support.
The deposited Pt will consist of sub-nanometer to few-nanometer clusters.
The controlled synthesis will produce a narrow Pt nanoparticle size distribution.
The controlled synthesis will create strong Pt-support interfacial bonding.
The high-entropy oxide support provides enhanced oxygen mobility.
The high-entropy oxide support provides structural stability that anchors Pt nanoparticles.
Anchoring Pt nanoparticles on the high-entropy oxide suppresses Pt sintering.
Pulse-controlled dropwise synthesis precisely controls Pt nucleation and growth at an ultrafine scale.
The disordered high-entropy oxide structure enhances oxygen-vacancy formation.
The high-entropy oxide enhances metal-support interactions.
Enhanced oxygen-vacancy formation and metal-support interactions improve oxidation kinetics.
The proposed structure reduces Pt aggregation during high-temperature redox cycling.
The proposed catalyst will have a significantly lower CO-oxidation T10 than conventionally impregnated Pt/Al2O3.
The proposed catalyst will maintain high catalytic activity during prolonged thermal and redox cycling.
The proposed catalyst will provide comparable or superior performance to conventional Pt/Al2O3 at substantially lower Pt loading.
The predicted benefits should hold under simulated automotive exhaust at 300–600 °C in cyclic redox and oxygen-rich atmospheres.
Synthesis scale-up or more extreme operating conditions may limit the predicted benefits.
